title: Washington and the Cherry Tree
text: When George Washington was a boy, he lived on a farm in Virginia. His father gave him a sharp new axe as a gift. George liked the axe very much. He went into the garden and cut a small cherry tree to see how the blade worked. The next morning, his father saw the broken tree. He was very angry. "Who cut my cherry tree?" he asked. For a moment, George wanted to hide the truth. But then he looked at his father and said, "I cannot tell a lie, Father. I cut the tree with my axe." His father's angry face became soft. "I am sad about the tree," he said, "but your honesty is worth more than a thousand trees." From that day on, George was known as a truthful boy who grew into a great leader.
translation: 乔治·华盛顿小时候住在弗吉尼亚的一个农场上。他的父亲送给他一把锋利的新斧头作为礼物。乔治非常喜欢这把斧头。他走进花园，砍倒了一棵小樱桃树，想试试斧刃有多快。第二天早上，父亲看到了被砍断的树，非常生气。"谁砍了我的樱桃树？"他问道。有那么一瞬间，乔治想隐瞒真相。但他看着父亲说："爸爸，我不能撒谎。是我用斧头砍了那棵树。"父亲愤怒的表情变得温和起来。"我为这棵树感到难过，"他说，"但你的诚实比一千棵树更有价值。"从那天起，乔治就以诚实的孩子而闻名，长大后成为了一位伟大的领袖。
